claim: For the positive-parameter quadratic flow \(\dot x=y\), \(\dot y=-a x+y z\), and \(\dot z=x^2-b y^2\), with \(a>0\) and \(b>0\), the divergence is exactly \(z\). For the equilibrium line \(E_s=(0,0,s)\), Liouville's formula gives \(\det D\phi_t(E_s)=e^{s t}\), so bounded trajectories realize every real asymptotic phase-volume rate \(s\). Consequently the vector field is not globally Lebesgue-volume preserving, and no positive \(C^1\) density can define an invariant smooth volume form on any open set containing a nonzero equilibrium \(E_s\). The transverse characteristic polynomial at \(E_s\) is \(\lambda^2-s\lambda+a\): its two transverse eigenvalues have negative real part for \(s<0\), positive real part for \(s>0\), and are purely imaginary at \(s=0\); nevertheless no individual point of the equilibrium line is asymptotically stable in the full phase space. Moreover every compactly supported invariant probability measure \(\mu\) satisfies \(\int x^2\,d\mu=b\int y^2\,d\mu\) and \(\int y^2 z\,d\mu=0\), with both quadratic moments zero exactly when \(\mu\) is supported on the equilibrium line. Thus the 2022 source paper's system-wide conclusion that the oscillator is conservative and has no dissipation does not follow from its single near-zero Lyapunov-sum trajectory; under the broader initial-condition-dependent taxonomy of conservative flows, individual zero-average-divergence trajectories remain possible but coexist with exact bounded trajectories having nonzero phase-volume rates.
integrity: The 2022 primary full text was inspected for publication date, vector field, numerical Lyapunov claim, equilibrium line, stability discussion, and conclusion. The 2019 conservative-flow taxonomy was inspected in full-text PDF, including its divergence criteria and initial-condition-dependent category. A packaged symbolic checker independently reconstructs the divergence, equilibrium Jacobian characteristic polynomial, and invariant-measure balance identities. No independent audit or external validation is claimed.
limitations: The theorem does not determine the time-average of z for the source article's particular chaotic initial condition, does not prove or refute chaos or multistability, and does not address a Hamiltonian or mechanical-energy formulation. The invariant-density obstruction assumes a positive C^1 density. The originality check is search-based and may miss unindexed equivalent work.
title: Exact phase-volume rates and invariant-measure balance in a line-equilibrium quadratic flow
